correctness.rationale: For every sorted quintuple of nonnegative integers and every n>=1, 0<=k<=n, reconstructs the three necessary B_f(2,1), B_f(3,1), B_f(4,2) tests, the exhaustive monotonic-rational prefix bound for the first test, and exact five-shift enumeration of 927939 prefix calls, 1323 first-test tuples, and eight survivors. For seven cases the nonincreasing multiplicities decompose into binomid Pascal-column factors. For the exceptional n^3(n+1)(n+3), the all-modulus floor-carry lemma has unique negative E_4(1,1)=-1, canceled at p=2,j=1 by E_2(1,1)=1; for all m>=6 the three zero shifts dominate both possible negative contributions, and m<=5 is handled explicitly. Legendre valuations then prove integrality of every B_f(n,k), not just checked rows. Independently recomputed the exhaustive enumeration and finite m<=100 checks, plus 8-tuples for n<=50; finite experiments corroborate the bound/lemma but are not the infinite proof.
residual_risks: Computer-assisted necessity needs executable exact-rational recursion and its explicit monotone bound; a finite enumeration without the bound is not a proof.
The modulo lemma is essential for the exceptional infinite case: finite checked moduli alone would not prove it.
No formal Lean or independent expert attestation has been performed.

value.rationale: The binomidness problem for positive integer-root polynomial factors is a naturally motivated extension of classical Pascal columns; a complete degree-five integer-shift classification replaces five freely varying shift parameters by exactly eight realizable multisets. Three fixed low-index integrality tests unexpectedly recognize all cases, and the one non-Pascal product reveals a genuine two-adic carry-compensation mechanism absent from monotone root multiplicities. This is a structural counterexample to the naive Pascal-product-only conjecture, and a useful exact test case for subsequent classifications; no claim for arbitrary quintic coefficients, higher iterates or noninteger shifts.
residual_risks: The classification is intentionally limited to five nonnegative integer root shifts and relies on a large exact finite recursion; it is not a classification of all degree-five binomid sequences.
Broader future utility has not been independently demonstrated, and narrower known special cases should not be represented as new.

final_claim: For sorted a_1<=...<=a_5 nonnegative integers and f(n)=product_i (n+a_i), binomidness at all n>=k>=0 is equivalent to integrality of B_f(2,1), B_f(3,1), B_f(4,2) and holds for exactly eight listed shift multisets; seven are Pascal-column products and the exceptional (0,0,0,1,3) f(n)=n^3(n+1)(n+3) is proved by two-adic carry compensation.
limitations: Five ordered nonnegative integer shifts only; does not cover general quintics, arbitrary rational/complex roots or iterated binomidness.
Computer-assisted exhaustive branch-and-bound necessity proof requires its exact coverage invariant.
Modulus checks m<=100 and index checks n<=50 do not establish all-modulus/infinite-index theorem.
Best-of-knowledge originality is qualified; no independent published certificate or expert/Lean attestation.
